newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Chemicals group Sentrachem announced a major restructuring aimed at cutting debt by one billion rand within 12 to 18 months. It might also lead to a listing of U.S.-based subsidiary Hampshire Chemical Corp in London or New York next year.
- Anglo American Platinum Mines (Amplats) has called for government intervention to assist in defusing violence at mines in the wake of the killing of two National Union of Mineworkers leaders.

- Industrial holding company Bidvest has bought all of stationery group Walton's business interests and trademarks through the issue of 28 million shares -- effectively putting a 966 million rand price tag on its biggest acquisition to date.
- The huge restructuring at Transnet subsidiary PX, which includes almost halving the parcel operator's staff, has led to major delivery backlogs, PX head Nico Heyns said.
- Namibia Breweries has accused South African Breweries of "bullying tactics" by attempting to disrupt the Namibian market with a non-refundable 750ml bottle.

- Securities Regulation Panel chairman Cyril Jaffe has proposed that the panel continue to regulate insider trading -- clashing with the view in the insider trading task group's majority draft report that the Financial Services Board take it over.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Gencor and the Industrial Development Corporation said they would go ahead with a 5.65 billion rand aluminium smelter in Maputo, the single largest direct foreign investment in Mozambique.
- The parastatal Development Bank of Southern Africa has raised 700 million rand to fund infrastructure projects by issuing more of its existing DV07 and DV06 bonds, the bank said.

- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all share and financial indices hit new highs on Tuesday as the market took heart from a firm rand and all but ignored Wall Street's second-largest one-day loss ever on Monday, dealers said.

- Bidvest, the trading and distribution group, has acquired the entire business undertakings and trademarks of Waltons as a going concern from Waltons Stationery in a deal valued at almost one billion rand, the company said.
- Khayelitsha township near Cape Town, could become the site of South Africa's first regional, small-business stock exchange, Clem Sunter, a director of Anglo American Corp said.
SAKE BEELD

- Gencor and the Industrial Development Corp have decided to go ahead with construction of an aluminium smelter in Maputo at a cost of $1.125 billion, including finance costs, on condition that international partners and financing is found.
- Absa has become the second banking group in a week to announce a cut in some of its fixed interest rates.
- Grootvlei mine, taken over earlier this year by the Harmony mining group, has called urgent meetings with labour unions to discuss rationalisation.
THE STAR

- The Truth and Reconciliation Commission is to subpoena President Nelson Mandela's former wife Winnie Madikizela-Mandela for questioning during a closed hearing about the activites for her notorious "Mandela United Football Club" in the 1980s.
- Thieves tried to steal a magistrate's car from the basement of the Hillbrow Magistrates' Court.
- Organisers of a countrywide road blockade to protest against crime are claiming a "victory of spirit" for Tuesday's anti-crime campaign, which largely failed to materialise.
- Banks are negotiating a new agreement with police to allow them to disclose amounts robbed in bank hold-ups.
